title: PantherBots cap off another great year | Local & State | lufkindailynews.com
text:
The Lufkin High School robotics club recently wrapped up another successful season with a trip to the FIRST world championship in Houston. 2026 marked the PantherBots’ fifth appearance at worlds in the last seven years, according to head mentor Robyn Segrest, who has guided the team through its entire 19-year existence.
“This all started with me and 15 kids,” Segrest said. “But now we have 10 mentors and 67 kids. We’ve gone to basically operating like a full company with different departments.”
The PantherBots won the team spirit award at the world championship, reflecting how team members work with each other in addition to what FIRST calls “gracious professionalism” — derived from the golden rule. The team seeks to be good competitors while showing kindness to other teams.
This year marked the team’s third straight with at least one blue banner won. The PantherBots won a district event in San Antonio this year, avenging their only loss on the way.
In one of the toughest district events in Texas, the PantherBots traveled up to Farmersville and finished sixth, also winning the quality award. They would go on to qualify for the UIL state championship and then make yet another appearance as one of 600 teams at the FIRST world championship in Houston, where students enjoyed competing and interacting with teams from Canada, to China, to Turkey and everywhere in between.
“While at the world championships, our students had the opportunity to interact and make friends with students from countries they have only learned about in school,” Segrest said. “Teams from countries that have never heard of our small town respect and enjoy interacting with our team both on the game field and in the stands.”
The team’s Expected Points Added ranking of 144.4 was its highest in program history, ranking 13th in the state. Out of 3,724 teams worldwide, the PantherBots ranked 278th.
The PantherBots have a few team traditions. For one, some members wear tutus at each contest in celebration of “women in STEM.” As such, the team consists of a nearly even share of each gender. The use of glitter is another team tradition, with conflicting stories on how it was born.
Segrest is particularly proud of the team’s well-rounded nature. Students in the robotics program, many of whom are involved in multiple extracurricular activities at the school, combine the core subjects of English, math and physics in their work on robots.
“They apply the engineering design process and advanced analytical skills to develop match strategies to win at district events and advance to the state and world championships,” Segrest said.
Segrest thanked the Gene Hass Foundation, Lockheed Martin, the LHS career technical education department, Lufkin ISD, Optimum and Siemens for sponsoring the team’s activities, including attendance at four three-day competitions.
“Solid Rock Family Church actually donated lunch for us every day at every competition,” Segrest said. “They also gave us snacks and water, and breakfast when we stayed in a hotel that didn’t provide it.”
Segrest also thanked the team’s mentors — including Caleb Beames, Michael Bourlon, Travis Garcia, Timothy and Halli Glasscock, Hunter Overholt, Jason Page, Gus Parra, Chad Robertson, and Dale and Tish Snyder — for volunteering their time to further the team’s goals. Those mentors all have full-time jobs, Segrest said, and their willingness to give their spare time to the team has been invaluable to its success.
Lufkin Middle School students A.J. Beames and Jacob Slack have also contributed to the team, through interviewing members of other teams on their “Robo Bros” podcast.
“We’re very thankful for all of them helping us to build not just robots but humans, too,” Segrest said.
“The truly remarkable thing is that while our team celebrates their success, they never lose their humility and continue to set higher goals for themselves each year. They identify with every student in our district and see themselves as ‘just the kids from Lufkin.’”
